items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude the actual seat-claim entry point**

On Linux, this pattern does not fix seat claiming when Claude invokes `herdr-agents`: that executable launches `actas-claim.sh` internally in a command substitution at `home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_herdr-agents:655-656`. Claude Code matches `excludedCommands` against the command line submitted to Bash, explicitly does not match scripts invoked internally, and keeps command substitutions sandboxed, so the child still cannot reach the herdr socket ([official `excludedCommands` documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#run-commands-outside-the-sandbox-with-excludedcommands)). Exclude or otherwise accommodate the actual top-level invocation instead; the rendering test cited by the threat table only checks that this ineffective string is emitted.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/a06f646f7b6f4386173ccec54e043331dd5c24bc/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update the sandbox documentation for Linux exclusions**

On Linux, these additions make `gh`, `herdr-agents`, and direct `actas-claim.sh` invocations run outside the sandbox, but `README.md:464-480` still says the only extra writable path is `~/.cache/uv`, allowed domains are GitHub-only, and `excludedCommands` contains only `agmsg-dispatch`. This leaves the repository's user-facing security documentation materially inconsistent with the applied policy; update that section alongside the configuration.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L71-L71](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/4498a2626003f5de789111c298ada8bc3d69ec12/AGENTS.md#L71-L71)
